evidence: On CPython 3.11.5, the submitted sealed reference passed all 4 public tests and all 10 sealed recovery tests.

Independent bounded runs passed for the reference model fuzzer at 600 operations, reference thread stress at 6 threads by 80 operations, reference torn-tail recovery, and the reference debugging regression; the intentionally buggy regression failed in the documented way.

The documented scripts/run_all.py, production/implementation/kvstore.py, and production/PRODUCTIONIZATION.md paths are absent from CANDIDATE, despite README instructions and MANIFEST claims for two alternatives and an instrumented variant.

Every documented production-target test, fuzz, stress, and fault-injection command failed because the production module is absent; a benchmark replay to /tmp also failed while loading the absent production implementation.

The archived benchmark reports production timings, but its production source is absent and PROVENANCE provides no run identity or submitted-tree hash, so those measurements cannot be reproduced or authenticated from this submission.

An independent boundary check stored three individually valid 1 MiB values, producing a 4194627-byte log, after which compact() raised ValueError: batch is too large, contradicting the unconditional compaction requirement.
An unterminated 4194305-byte tail, one byte above MAX_RECORD_BYTES, was accepted and truncated to zero; replay reads the entire file before applying its record-size check.

Solution code, hidden tests, the debugging root cause and patch, and the expected code review are directly readable inside the submitted archive; no enforced learner-view or reveal boundary is included.

The pinned local Build Your Own X commit exists, contains the cited DBDB catalog link, and states a CC0 waiver; the linked tutorial license and the license of the generated candidate material are not separately established.

limitations: The absent production implementation prevents any independent conclusion about its correctness, instrumentation, fuzzing, stress behavior, fault recovery, or performance.
The archived benchmark cannot be rerun from this submission, and its historical execution identity and exact implementation hashes are unavailable.
The fault-injection script models a torn tail after a clean close; no real process crash, power loss, filesystem fault, or cross-platform durability campaign was performed.
The linked external tutorial was not fetched, so its license and any textual or code similarity to generated material remain unverified.
Thread stress and fuzzing were single bounded deterministic runs and do not establish exhaustive concurrency or corruption safety.
The archive does not include a generated learner view, so disclosure safety was assessed from the directly readable submitted tree rather than an independently staged student package.
